newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Rate on Yugoslav cen.bank bonds hits record high.
newsitem.headline: Rate on Yugoslav cen.bank bonds hits record high.

text.p: The Yugoslav central bank set the interest rate for short-term bonds it auctioned on Wednesday at a record high 128.29 percent, the Belgrade bourse said.
This compares to the 122.29 percent rate set for the previous tranche of bonds, auctioned on October 7. The lowest rate ever on those securities stood at 60.7 percent.
The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) offered at today's auction a new 30 million dinar ($6 million) tranche of 30-day bonds, but sold only 1.8 million dinars worth, the bourse said.
Buying interest was low because of tightening bank sector liquidity and expectations the reserve requirement will rise to 15 from 10 percent.
Commercial banks have largely neglected NBY short-term bonds ever since the central bank tightened its stance and launched the reserve requirement.
A source close to the market cited delays in payment operations within the banking sector as a possible drag on today's bond auction. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
